config.title: Shows in Berlin in English - FAQ
config.subtitle: Which Berlin stages work without German, what the surtitle system actually is, and what a theatre night costs.

items.q: Can I enjoy a theatre show in Berlin without speaking German?
items.a: Yes, in three ways. **Visual shows carry no language at all**: the Grand Show at Friedrichstadt-Palast, contemporary circus at Chamäleon, and varieté at Wintergarten. **Several major theatres surtitle German performances in English**: Maxim Gorki Theater does it for its German-language productions apart from premieres, and the Berliner Ensemble, Schaubühne and Deutsches Theater mark surtitled dates in their calendars. And **English Theatre Berlin plus the English comedy scene play in English outright**.

items.q: What are English surtitles and do they cost extra?
items.a: Surtitles are a **live English translation projected on a screen above or beside the stage** while the actors perform in German. They cost nothing extra; you buy a normal ticket for a performance marked with English surtitles. At the **Berliner Ensemble, sit in the balconies or from row 13 in the stalls** so the surtitle screen and the stage stay in one line of sight. The Schaubühne also offers surtitles you can read on your own phone in flight mode at some performances.

items.q: How much do Berlin shows cost?
items.a: Roughly three bands. **Subsidised theatres are the bargain**: normal seats commonly land between about EUR 10 and 50, and the Berliner Ensemble sells student tickets for EUR 9. **The big visual shows cost more**: Chamäleon runs roughly EUR 40 to 72, and autumn dates for the Friedrichstadt-Palast Grand Show were selling from about EUR 64 on the major ticket platforms when I checked on 2 September 2026. **English comedy nights are the cheapest**, often around the price of two drinks.

items.q: Is the Friedrichstadt-Palast show in German?
items.a: It barely matters. The Grand Show is a **visual spectacle of costumes, acrobatics and music with no plot dialogue to follow**, on the largest theatre stage in Europe. **BLINDED by DELIGHT premiered in October 2025** and runs until June 2027, about 2.5 hours with interval. It is back from 3 September after the summer break. Non-German speakers fill the hall every night.

items.q: Is Blue Man Group still playing in Berlin?
items.a: **No. Blue Man Group closed at the end of 2025** after 18 years at the Stage Bluemax Theater on Potsdamer Platz. The venue now hosts changing productions, mostly in German. Plenty of older guides and roundups still list it, so double-check before you plan an evening around it; the closest current no-language alternatives are the Friedrichstadt-Palast Grand Show and Chamäleon.
